contents.reason: Double complexes introduce a second grading, two anticommuting differentials, and totalization choices that the present pair does not need. The live plan gives them their own later A/B pair rather than smuggling them into HA-2.

contents.name: Sign Trick 1.2.5
contents.reason: The sign trick belongs to the double-complex page, where it is used to identify bicomplexes with complexes in Ch(A) and to control total-complex signs. Nothing in this pair depends on that two-direction bookkeeping.

contents.name: Total Complexes 1.2.6
contents.reason: Total complexes become load-bearing only when cones, spectral sequences, and Grothendieck constructions start assembling bicomplexes. This pair stays at ordinary chain complexes, homotopies, and the quotient category K(A).

contents.name: Truncations 1.2.7
contents.reason: Brutal and canonical truncations are not used to define chain homotopy or K(A). The live plan assigns them to the later derived-categories page together with the canonical t-structure and truncation triangles.
